title: Efficient On-Device Inference for Large Language Models via Structured Sparsity
summary: We present SparseServe, a method for running large language models on consumer hardware. By combining structured 2:4 sparsity with 4-bit quantization, SparseServe achieves a 3.2x inference speedup over the dense FP16 baseline while retaining task accuracy. On the MMLU benchmark, our 7B-parameter model reaches 68.4% accuracy, within 1.1 points of the dense model at one third of the memory footprint. We release the code and quantized weights under a permissive license.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Verified Citations
summary: Hallucinated citations remain a barrier to deploying retrieval-augmented generation in high-stakes settings. We introduce a span-verification gate that rejects any generated claim whose supporting quote does not appear verbatim in a retrieved source. On a held-out factual-QA set the gate reduces unsupported claims from 14.2% to 0.4% with a 2.1-point drop in answered-question coverage. The approach is model-agnostic and adds no additional training.
